from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Slope is change in y over change in x.", "Secant lines measure average change.", "Points on a curve connect to show interval."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The Average Rate of Change", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 6, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2*x**2 + 1, x_range=[0, 5], color=BLUE)
        
        p1 = axes.coords_to_point(1, 1.2)
        p2 = axes.coords_to_point(4, 4.2)
        
        dot1 = Dot(p1, color=YELLOW)
        dot2 = Dot(p2, color=YELLOW)
        secant = Line(p1, p2, color=RED)
        
        graph = VGroup(axes, curve, dot1, dot2, secant)
        self.place_in_area(graph, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(Create(dot1), Create(dot2))
        self.play(Create(secant))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Indicate(dot1), Indicate(dot2))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Zoom in to see the interval shrink.", 
            "As dx approaches zero, it transforms.", 
            "Secant line becomes a tangent line.", 
            "Average speed becomes instantaneous speed.", 
            "Limit identifies the exact rate of change."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Transformation: The Limit of Shrinkage", lecture_lines)

        p1 = axes.c2p(0.5, 0.625)
        p2 = axes.c2p(2.0, 2.5)

        secant = Line(p1, p2, color=RED)
        
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, graph, dot1, dot2, secant)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "A2", "F5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(graph_group.animate.scale(1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(dot2.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(1.0, 1.0)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        tangent = TangentLine(graph, alpha=0.5, length=3, color=GREEN)
        self.play(FadeIn(tangent))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Indicate(tangent))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Geometric Interpretation: Dynamic Tangency", [
            "Derivative is the slope function.",
            "It shows direction at every point.",
            "Path slope equals instantaneous velocity.",
            "Derivative captures precise orientation.",
            "Dynamic tangency defines the curve behavior."

        self.place_in_area(circle, 'B2', 'E5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene, MovingCameraScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Curves look linear when zoomed in.",
            "Derivative provides local linear approximation.",
            "Use linear math for complex paths.",
            "Predict position using velocity vectors.",
            "Motion behaves linearly at any instant."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Derivative as a Local Linearization", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create objects
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3*x) + 0.2 * x**2, x_range=[-2, 2], color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.move_to(curve.point_from_proportion(0.5))
        
        # Tangent line (initially invisible)
        tangent = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=RED).scale(0.5)
        tangent.move_to(dot.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(curve), FadeIn(dot))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(self.camera.frame.animate.set(zoom=2).move_to(dot.get_center()))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(Create(tangent))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        vector = Arrow(start=dot.get_center(), end=dot.get_center() + RIGHT*0.5 + UP*0.2, color=ORANGE)
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Derivative is instantaneous rate of change.",
            "It is the slope of a tangent.",
            "Curves are series of linear segments."
        ])
        
        # Animation Elements
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3*x) + 0.5 * x**2, x_range=[-1, 2], color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        tangent_line = Line(start=LEFT*1, end=RIGHT*1, color=RED).rotate(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(tangent_line, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(tangent_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        # Create series of segments
        segments = VGroup()
        for i in range(10):
            x = -0.8 + i * 0.3
            y = 0.5 * np.sin(3*x) + 0.5 * x**2
            seg = Line(start=np.array([x, y, 0]), end=np.array([x+0.2, y+0.1, 0]), color=WHITE)
            segments.add(seg)
        self.place_in_area(segments, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(curve), FadeOut(tangent_line))
        self.play(Create(segments))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: From Static to Dynamic
outline.target_audience: University students (Calculus I or Physics I)

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Average Rate of Change
sections.content: Recall the slope formula: m = Δy / Δx. Visually represent this as a secant line connecting two points on a curve, representing 'average' change over an interval.
sections.example: A cheetah running between two trees: measuring its average speed by dividing total distance by total time.

sections.title: The Transformation: The Limit of Shrinkage
sections.content: Introduce the 'zoom-in' concept. As the interval Δx approaches zero, the secant line transforms into a tangent line. This is the transition from 'average' to 'instantaneous'.
sections.example: Visualizing a high-speed camera frame-by-frame zoom on the cheetah's paw position; as the frames get closer, we isolate the exact speed at one specific millisecond.

sections.title: The Geometric Interpretation: Dynamic Tangency
sections.content: Explain the derivative as the 'slope function'. If the curve represents a path, the derivative represents the 'steering direction' or instantaneous orientation at every point.
sections.example: A robotic arm tracing a circular path; the derivative represents the precise angle of the arm's velocity vector at every point on the circle.

sections.title: Application: The Derivative as a Local Linearization
sections.content: Summarize the transformation: complex nonlinear curves look like simple straight lines when viewed under a 'microscope' of a derivative. This allows us to use simple linear math to predict complex paths.
sections.example: Predicting the flight path of a bird: even though the bird's path is curved, at any tiny moment, we treat its motion as a linear velocity vector to predict its next position.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the shift: Derivative = Rate of Change = Slope of Tangent = Local Linearization. Final visual: An animation showing a curve morphing into a series of tiny connected line segments.
sections.example: Comparing the cheetah's smooth, curved hunting path to a series of connected straight-line 'velocity vectors' derived from the path's derivative.
